newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee may push down, uptrend broken.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee may push down, uptrend broken.

text.p: MAY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Coffee broke an uptrend that had lasted since January on Friday, and may be set for a push down, analysts said.
"Last week it pretty well traded sideways, but we might see a slightly more decisive push lower," Adrian Haylor, analyst at Sucden, said.
Moving averages that were above the market added to the bearish weight, he said.
Traders called coffee to open $20 to $30 lower.
Haylor put initial support at $1,529 a tonne, with further points at $1,515 and then $1,460. He put resistance at $1,668.
In New York on Friday a late-session sell-off by commission houses ahead of the weekend sent CSCE coffee prices mostly lower by the close, dealers said.
On the fundamental side, a report by the Mexican Coffee Council showed the country's coffee exports totalled 651,495 60-kg bags in March, up from the 631,513 sent abroad in the same month in 1996.
Analysts and traders said many Latin American countries had shipped heavily during the past two months to take advantage of the higher prices on the futures exchange.
Uganda said on Friday it would export 4.4 million 60-kg bags of coffee in 1996/97 compared with 4.1 million in 1995/96.
Also on Friday, Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation raised the country's internal coffee price by 0.8 percent to 342,750 pesos per 125-kg load, a spokesman said.
